title: The Whole Robot for a Day: Built, Gated, Shipped, Driven Through Its Faults and Reported, With the Black Box to Say What Happened

questions.question: Which line of the day's report is the one a reader trusts it for?
options: The totals, which show how many jobs were delivered
The version line, which shows the gate passed
The last: the hazards with no scenario, which says what nobody has shown, where a report ending on the good news is a report of a good day
The black box line, which shows the log is intact
questions.explanation: A report that ended on the good news would be a report of a good day. The last line says which hazards nobody has shown anything about.

questions.question: The unsafe rover had the better day by one measure. Which, and what were the others?
options: Bumps: it had fewer
Battery: it used less
Operator resets: it needed more
Deliveries, 5 of 5 against 3, with 288 bumps, no stops where two were needed and no resets
questions.explanation: It delivered all five, including the two jobs where stopping was right, and was in contact for 288 ticks. By the first number a customer sees, it won.

questions.question: Why does the day have two operator resets?
options: The gate was run twice
Two jobs ended in a latched stop by the supervisor (link and sensors), and a latched stop needs a person
The black box filled up twice
Two jobs took too long
questions.explanation: The link was lost in one job and the sensor died in another. Each is a latched stop, and a latched stop is cleared by a person.

questions.question: The gate refused the release. What was the robot's day?
options: A bad one: nothing was delivered
The same as before: still on 1.4.2, 3 delivered, 2 stopped, 0 bumps
An idle one: the robot waited for a release
An unsafe one, on the refused policy
questions.explanation: Nothing was written to the robot. It ran the policy it already had and had the same day as before.

questions.question: What does 'chain verified' on the black box line tell a reader?
options: The robot is safe
The log is complete to the last event
The log has not been edited between the robot and the report: a missing, reordered or altered event would be found
The clock was right all day
questions.explanation: Each event carries a hash of itself and the one before. A change, a removal or a reordering between the robot and the report would break the chain.

questions.question: What can this report not claim?
options: Reliability: it is one day of five jobs in one simulated building, and it can only show what the suite tries
How many jobs were delivered
Why each stop happened
Which release ran
questions.explanation: Five jobs in one simulated building is a sample. It shows what happened on this day in these cases, and nothing about the days and cases it did not have.
